text:
alexa (People Ops): Quick heads-up — two coordinated changes coming May 1: 1) Time-off eligibility rules clarified for part-time and contractors; 2) Were launching a Redwood Travel Medical Card for business trips (global coverage tiers). TL;DR below, details after.

alexa (People Ops): TL;DR: part-time employees who average >=20 hrs/wk are now eligible for the same accrual schedule as full-time after a 60-day eligibility window. Contractors on >6mo engagements get a prorated wellness day allocation (not full PTO). Travel Medical Card: company-paid card for emergency medical expenses while traveling on company business; request via Travel Portal, card shipped or virtual depending on region.

alexa (People Ops): Why: we heard many folks asking for consistent coverage on business travel and clearer rules for folks working flexible schedules. These changes reduce confusion and speed approvals.

jordan (Eng): Does the 60-day window apply retroactively to folks who started Jan/Feb?
mike (Benefits): Good Q — eligibility is evaluated from employment start date. If youve already passed 60 days before May 1, your accrual schedule is effective immediately on May 1. If you hit 60 days after May 1, accrual changes when the 60-day mark is reached. Well run a payroll sync and update balances automatically.
natalie (Sales): For the Travel Medical Card — does it cover routine care or only emergencies? And what about pre-existing conditions?
mike (Benefits): The card covers emergency medical, urgent care, and medically necessary evacuation in extreme cases. It does NOT replace personal health insurance; routine care and elective procedures are excluded. Pre-existing conditions are covered for emergencies but treatment for the condition that was planned prior to travel is not covered. Full policy: https://console.redwood.com/policies/travel-medical (internal).
natalie (Sales): Cool, thanks. How do I get one before an upcoming client trip next week?
alexa (People Ops): If travel is company-approved, submit a Travel Card request in the Travel Portal by selecting your trip and clicking "Request Card". For trips <7 days we issue a virtual card (email + in-app) within 24 hours; for longer or repeated international travel we ship a physical card (ETA depends on region). If you need expedited card shipping, ping me with the trip ID.

ops-bot: Updated doc posted: /policies/timeoff-and-travel-medical (link) — version v1.2 published 2026-05-01.
mike (Benefits): A few quick callouts for managers: - Check team member eligibility in People Admin before approving time off. - Contractors: use the new contractor accrual calculator (link in the policy). - For travel medical card expenses: keep receipts and file expense reports under category "Travel Medical". Card transactions automatically attach to the trip ID.
jordan (Eng): Any change in carryover limits or blackout windows?
alexa (People Ops): No changes to carryover caps this round. We did tighten the blackout exception process for end-of-year — managers must file a business case for exceptions >3 days during product freeze windows.
natalie (Sales): Are there region-specific disclaimers? I'm based in EU.
mike (Benefits): Yes — the Travel Medical Card has region-specific network partners. For EU/UK we use MedAssistEU; APAC has separate network and shipping rules. The policy includes a per-region appendix and emergency hotline numbers.
alexa (People Ops): FAQ drop: we'll run two short AMA sessions next Wed/Thu (15 min) — calendar invites going out in Slack. If you have immediate questions, DM me or open a ticket at #help > "Timeoff & Travel Benefits". :thumbsup:
natalie (Sales): thanks — will join the AMA. :raised_hands:
alexa (People Ops): Appended note: if youre a manager with direct reports on flexible schedules and want a team-level review before May 1, book a 30-min slot with People Ops: /calendar/book/alexa.

jordan (Eng): appreciate the clarity, thanks!
